newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Arco holds 56 pct of Venezuela field deal.
newsitem.headline: Arco holds 56 pct of Venezuela field deal.

text.p: U.S. oil company Atlantic Richfield Co (Arco) holds a 56 percent share in the consortium that successfully bid for Venezuela's Kaki marginal oil field Monday, a spokesman said.
The consortium, which includes Venezuelan companies Inelectra with a 30 percent stake and leading local foods group Polar with a 14 percent share, paid $60 million for the field in eastern Venezuela.
"We're very happy," Arco president John Cheatham said in a press conference after the auction.
Among the 14 bidders, the lowest offer came in at $500,000 from a consortium of Canada's Norcen and Venezuela's Flag Instalaciones.
A source at state oil company PDVSA said the Kaki field currently produced around 1,000 barrels per day (BPD), although production could rise to 30,000 bpd.
Under the 20-year contract, the operator will produce hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Corpoven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale.

Discovered in 1957, Kaki was one of five areas reserved for Venezuelan operators with a minimum 30 percent stake. As a condition of the contract, the operator must invest at least $7 million within three years.
The auction was the first in Venezuela's third round of oil operating contract auctions in which a total of 131 companies are competing for 20 contracts.
